newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Key dates since Rabin's assassination.
newsitem.headline: Key dates since Rabin's assassination.

text.p: Key dates since the assassination of Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin a year ago:
- Nov 4, 1995: Gunman Yigal Amir, right-wing Jew opposed to Israeli peace moves, kills Rabin. His Labour party comrade, Foreign Minister Shimon Peres, becomes Israeli prime minister.
- Dec 27: Israel cedes control of Ramallah, completing handover to Palestinian self-rule of six West Bank towns under September accord signed by Rabin.

- Jan 5, 1996: Yahya Ayyash, elusive mastermind behind wave of Palestinian suicide bombings, is killed in PLO-ruled Gaza. Militant Hamas group vows to retaliate against Israel for killing of Ayyash, nicknamed "The Engineer".
- Jan 20: Palestinians hold first election for president and parliament to West Bank and Gaza under peace deal Rabin signed. PLO Chairman Yasser Arafat elected president.
- Feb 11: Prime Minister Peres, way ahead of challenger Benjamin Netanyahu in opinion polls, says he will call general election as soon as law allows.
- Feb 20: Israel's main political parties end week of bickering, setting May 29 as date for early elections.
- Feb 25 to March 4: Moslem militant suicide bombers from Hamas carry out four attacks, killing 59 people in Israel. Peres falls in polls; race is neck-and-neck.
- March 27: Amir jailed for life for Rabin's murder.
- March 28: Official Israeli inquiry into assassination finds security officials ignored intelligence information suggesting Jewish militant might try to kill prime minister.
- April 26: United States announces limited ceasefire ending 17 days of fighting between Israeli forces and Hizbollah guerrillas on both sides of Israel-Lebanon border.
- May 29: Israelis elect Netanyahu prime minister.
- Aug 2: Netanyahu's right-wing government paves way for expanding Jewish settlements in occupied lands, ending four-year freeze imposed by Rabin and angering Palestinians.
- Sept 24: Netanyahu opens a new entrance to an archaeological tunnel in Arab East Jerusalem, angering Palestinians and touching off four days of clashes in which 60 Arabs and 15 Israelis are killed.
- Oct 3: Amir, his brother, and third religious Jew are jailed for five to 12 years for plotting Rabin's murder.

- Oct 24: Israelis mark year to Rabin assassination according to Jewish calendar as divided politically as ever. Grandson Yonatan Ben-Artzi asks Rabin's forgiveness at gravesite saying: "A year has passed and nothing has changed."
- Oct 31: Netanyahu and Arafat have yet to seal accord on Israeli pullout from Hebron, last of seven West Bank cities due to be handed over to PLO under 1995 deal signed by Rabin.
